The makespan of a randomly chosen complete schedule.

Ready time is exactly the starting point; dropping it would make the estimate inaccurate and unsafe.
A dish's remaining steps must run in order, so its ready time plus the duration if every step got the fastest chef gives an optimistic, safe bound.

scenario: branch-and-bound 在最小化 makespan，手上已有一个合法 best，而下界是绝不高估的乐观估计。
scenario_en: Branch-and-bound is minimizing makespan, you already hold a valid best, and the bound is an optimistic estimate that never overestimates.
q: 搜索中为什么可以在 `bound >= best_makespan` 时剪枝？
q_en: Why can search prune when `bound >= best_makespan`?
options: 乐观下界追不上当前 best，此分支不可能更优
下界越大代表 schedule 质量越好
best_makespan 是一个随机生成的数字
剪枝会跳过所有候选，但仍保证得到新的 best
options_en: Even the optimistic bound cannot beat the current best, so this branch cannot produce a better complete schedule.
A larger bound always means a better-quality schedule.
best_makespan is just a randomly generated number.
Pruning skips every candidate but still guarantees a new best.
why: 目标是最小化 makespan；下界已经不小于当前最优时，继续搜索只会浪费时间。
why_en: If the optimistic bound cannot beat the incumbent, no completion in that branch can improve the answer.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Partial state] --> B[Compute optimistic bound]
B --> C{Can beat best?}
C -->|yes| D[Search children]
C -->|no| E[Prune branch]

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 搜索过程中当前已知的最好完整解，后续分支要击败它才有意义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The incumbent is the best complete solution found so far, and later branches only matter if they can beat it.

optionExplanations: 下界是这条分支最好也只能做到的程度，连这个乐观值都追不上已知最好解，继续往下搜纯属浪费。
下界大小只是估计值，跟排出来的 schedule 好不好没有必然关系。
best_makespan 是搜索过程中实际找到的最好解，不是随便生成的数字。
剪枝只是跳过没希望的分支，不会凭空产出新的更好解，也不保证一定找到 new best。
optionExplanations_en: The bound is the best this branch could possibly reach, and if even that optimistic value can't beat the known best, searching further just wastes time.
A bigger bound value is just an estimate -- it doesn't mean the resulting schedule is actually better.
best_makespan is the best solution actually found during the search, not some arbitrary number.
Pruning only skips hopeless branches; it doesn't conjure a better solution out of nowhere or guarantee a new best.

scenario: 示例 chef 速度中，每个 station 都有一个 0.5 factor specialist，其他人是 1.5 factor。
scenario_en: In the sample chef speeds, each station has one 0.5-factor specialist while the others run at a 1.5 factor.
q: 搜索版如何利用这个结构降低分支？
q_en: How does the search version use this structure to reduce branching?
options: 为每个 step 都依然枚举所有可能的 chef 与 station 的完整组合方式
把 chef 固定为该 station 的 specialist，只搜索 step 顺序
随机挑一个手速较慢的 non-specialist 厨师顶上去做这一步
让唯一一个厨师一个人包办这整单里的所有 step 工作
options_en: Still enumerate every combination of chef and station for each step.
Pin each step's chef to that station's specialist, and search only the step order.
Randomly substitute in whichever non-specialist chef happens to be slower.
Let a single chef single-handedly take on every step in the whole order.
why: 在这些实例里 non-specialist 慢三倍且不值得用，chef 维度可以折叠，真正的选择留给 ordering。
why_en: The specialist structure collapses chef choice so the search can focus on ordering.
whenOtherWins: 如果非 specialist 在排队压力下可能比等待 specialist 更早完成，就必须重新把 chef choice 纳入搜索。
tradeoff: 把 chef 折叠成 specialist、只搜 ordering vs 每步都枚举 chef+station

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 station 上速度是 0.5 factor 的 chef，比其余 1.5 factor 的 chef 快三倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialist is the one chef who runs a given station at half the base time, three times faster than a non-specialist there.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在给定结构下必然不比另一个候选更优，可以直接排除而不影响最优解的选项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dominated choice can never beat another option given the problem's structure, so it can be excluded without affecting optimality.

optionExplanations: 还枚举每个 chef 和 station 没有利用这个结构，分支数量没有被压缩。
厨师选择在本例里没有悬念，把它钉死在专精厨师上，搜索树就只剩下步骤怎么排这一个维度。
随便换成一个不擅长这个 station 的厨师，等于主动引入一个已知更慢的选择，没有道理这么做。
让一个厨师包办所有 step 会违反同一时刻只能做一件事的约束，根本不合法。
optionExplanations_en: Still enumerating every chef and station doesn't exploit this structure at all -- branching stays just as large.
Chef choice has no suspense in this example -- pin it to the specialist, and the search tree shrinks down to just step ordering.
Swapping in whichever chef is weaker at this station deliberately picks a choice already known to be worse, with no upside.
Letting one chef handle every step would break the one-step-at-a-time constraint and simply isn't legal.

scenario: order 里有多个 dish 使用相同 recipe，且它们处在相同步骤、相同 ready time。
scenario_en: The order has multiple dishes with the same recipe, the same step progress, and the same ready time.
q: 搜索如何避免重复等价分支？
q_en: How does search avoid repeated equivalent branches?
options: 把所有重复 recipe 的 dish 全部跳过不排入 schedule
随意改动其中一个 dish 的 recipe 内容
只探索一个代表，跳过 recipe/进度/ready time 全同的候选
把这些 dish 强行合并成一个更大的 dish
options_en: Delete every dish that shares a repeated recipe and never schedule it.
Randomly change one of the duplicate dishes' recipe.
Explore only one representative, skipping candidates identical in recipe, progress, and ready time.
Force these dishes to merge into one larger dish.
why: 这些 dish 在未来搜索中可互换，尝试每一个会产生同构子树；symmetry cut 保留一个代表即可。
why_en: Interchangeable dishes lead to identical subtrees, so the search only needs one representative.
whenOtherWins: 如果两个 dish 虽 recipe 相同但 deadline、优先级或 ready time 不同，就不能合并。
tradeoff: symmetry cut：只探索一个代表 vs 把每个可互换 dish 都单独搜索一遍

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一道 dish 内部固定顺序的 station step 链，后一步必须等前一步完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recipe is a dish's fixed chain of station steps, where each step must wait for the previous one to finish.

optionExplanations: 把这些菜整个跳过不排，等于漏掉了它们必须完成的工作，会产出不完整的 schedule。
随意改动其中一份菜谱会破坏这道菜原本的定义，跟对称剪枝没关系。
recipe、进度、ready time 完全相同的候选会展开出结构一样的子树，只探索其中一个代表、跳过其余等价候选——这就是 symmetry cut。
把几道菜强行并成一道会丢掉它们本该分别完成、分别计入 makespan 的事实。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping these dishes entirely would mean their required work never gets scheduled, producing an incomplete schedule.
Randomly editing one duplicate's recipe would break that dish's actual definition, unrelated to symmetry pruning.
Candidates identical in recipe, progress, and ready time expand into structurally identical subtrees, so exploring just one representative and skipping the rest is exactly what a symmetry cut does.
Forcibly merging several dishes into one would lose the fact that each must finish separately and count separately toward makespan.

scenario: deep_nine 用例要在 2.5 秒预算内跑完，而同一个 canonical 状态会从不同分支被反复到达。
scenario_en: The deep_nine case must finish inside a 2.5-second budget, and the same canonical state keeps getting reached down different branches.
q: branch-and-bound 的 memo 用来跳过什么？
q_en: What does the branch-and-bound memo skip?
options: 所有未完成的搜索状态
所有 makespan 比当前更小的状态
所有包含 Pasta 的搜索状态
已经以同等或更好下界见过的等价状态
options_en: Every unfinished search state.
Every state whose makespan is smaller than the current one.
Every state that happens to include Pasta.
Equivalent states already seen with an equal or better bound.
why: 如果同一 canonical 状态曾以更好下界出现，当前分支不会带来新希望；memo 减少重复搜索。
why_en: The memo skips repeated states already reached with an equal or better bound.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Canonical state key] --> B[Seen before?]
B -->|no| C[Store bound and search]
B -->|yes| D{Old bound no worse?}
D -->|yes| E[Skip state]
D -->|no| C

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存已搜索过的等价状态与当时的下界，命中时跳过重复搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memo caches equivalent states already searched along with the bound seen then, so the search can skip duplicate work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 跳过所有还没搜完的状态会把还有希望的分支也一起丢掉，这不是 memo 该做的事。
makespan 更小的状态往往正是更值得继续搜的，跳过它们反而会漏掉更优解。
题目里没有专门针对某道具体菜的规则，这个说法是编出来的。
同一个 canonical 状态如果之前已经以同等或更好的下界出现过，现在这个分支就不会有新发现，memo 跳过的正是这些重复状态。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping every unfinished state would throw away branches that still have promise -- that's not what a memo does.
States with a smaller makespan are often exactly the ones worth continuing to search, so skipping them risks missing a better answer.
There's no rule here specific to any one dish -- that claim is made up.
If the same canonical state was already seen with an equal or better bound, this branch can't offer anything new, and that's exactly what the memo skips.

scenario: 你在 search 中计算了当前状态的 lower bound，并准备查 memo。
scenario_en: In search, you computed the current state's lower bound and are about to check the memo.
q: `memo.get(key, inf) <= bound` 为什么可以剪？
q_en: Why can `memo.get(key, inf) <= bound` prune?
options: 同状态曾以不差的下界搜过，此分支无新信息
下界越大越好，越大越优先探索
key 里其实只记录了 dish 的名字
memo 只用来给最终输出排序
options_en: The same state was already searched with a bound at least as good, so this branch adds nothing new.
A bigger bound is always better and should be explored first.
The key only records the dish names.
The memo is only used to sort the final output.
codeSample:
key = (canonical(next_step, dish_ready), chef_free, station_free)
if memo.get(key, float("inf")) <= bound:
    return
memo[key] = bound
why: memo 记录到达等价状态时见过的最好下界，更差或相同下界的重复状态不用再展开。
why_en: The memo prunes duplicate states when an equal or stronger bound has already been explored.
whenOtherWins: 如果 key 缺少资源空闲时间等关键状态，剪枝会不安全。
tradeoff: 命中 memo 直接剪枝 vs 每次都重新展开等价状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存已搜索过的等价状态与当时的下界，命中时跳过重复搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memo caches equivalent states already searched along with the bound seen then, so the search can skip duplicate work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可互换的 dish 排序归一化后得到的状态标识，让 memo 能识别对称状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A canonical key normalizes interchangeable dishes into one sorted form so the memo can recognize symmetric states.

optionExplanations: 同一状态之前已经以不差的下界出现过，再展开一次不会挖到新信息，这行代码剪的就是这种重复。
下界只是乐观估计，越大不代表越好，反而可能意味着这个分支希望更小。
key 里还包含了 chef_free、station_free 这些资源信息，不只是 dish 名字。
memo 是用来剪枝、避免重复搜索的，不是给最终结果排序用的。
optionExplanations_en: This state was already seen before with a bound at least as good, so expanding it again adds nothing -- that's exactly the duplicate this line prunes.
A bound is just an optimistic estimate; a larger value doesn't mean better, if anything it can mean the branch has less promise.
The key also carries chef_free and station_free, not just dish names.
The memo exists to prune and avoid repeated search, not to order the final output.

scenario: 重复 recipe 的 dish 可以互换，但原始 dish index 不同。
scenario_en: Dishes with repeated recipes are interchangeable, but their original dish indexes differ.
q: `canonical(next_step, dish_ready)` 为什么要排序 signature、step、ready time？
q_en: Why does `canonical(next_step, dish_ready)` sort by signature, step, and ready time?
options: 让 schedule 按 dish 名字字母序输出
把可互换 dish 的进度归一化成同一个状态 key
计算每个 station 的 fastest chef
删除 dish 之间的前置关系
options_en: Sort the schedule output alphabetically by dish name.
Normalize interchangeable dishes' progress into one shared state key.
Compute the fastest chef for each station.
Delete the precedence relationship between dishes.
codeSample: return tuple(sorted((signature[d], next_step[d], dish_ready[d]) for d in range(len(dishes))))
why: 不同 dish index 但同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time 的状态等价；排序后 memo 能命中这些对称状态。
why_en: Canonicalizing interchangeable dishes lets the memo recognize symmetric states.
whenOtherWins: 如果 dish 有不同订单 id 约束或不同 deadline，canonical key 需要保留这些差异。
tradeoff: canonical key 归一化对称 dish vs 保留每个 dish 独立的原始 index

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可互换的 dish 排序归一化后得到的状态标识，让 memo 能识别对称状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A canonical key normalizes interchangeable dishes into one sorted form so the memo can recognize symmetric states.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

optionExplanations: 这行代码跟最终怎么打印 schedule 没关系，它服务的是搜索内部的状态识别。
把 recipe、进度、ready time 排序打包成一个 key，让原本 dish index 不同但其实等价的状态归到同一个 key 下，方便 memo 命中——这就是它的作用。
计算每个 station 最快厨师是另一套逻辑，跟这里的排序无关。
dish 之间的前置关系还在别处继续生效，这行代码并没有把它删掉。
optionExplanations_en: This line has nothing to do with how the final schedule gets printed -- it's about recognizing state equivalence inside the search.
Sorting recipe, progress, and ready time into one key lets states that differ only by dish index but are otherwise identical collapse into the same key -- exactly what lets the memo hit them.
Figuring out each station's fastest chef is separate logic, unrelated to this sorting step.
Precedence between dishes still holds elsewhere in the search; this line doesn't remove it.

scenario: 剪枝强度取决于多快拿到好的 incumbent；候选顺序不影响正确性，只影响搜索多快收敛。
scenario_en: Pruning strength depends on how fast you find a good incumbent, and candidate order changes only speed, never correctness.
q: branch-and-bound 里为什么还要把 candidates 按 `(end, d)` 排序？
q_en: Why does branch-and-bound still sort candidates by `(end, d)`?
options: 候选排序本身就足以证明这份 schedule 是最优的
不做排序就完全无法生成一份合法的 schedule
先试早完成候选，更快找到好 incumbent，加强剪枝
候选排序会彻底替代 lower bound 该起的作用
options_en: The ordering of candidates by itself is enough to prove the schedule is optimal.
Without sorting candidates, the search cannot produce a legal schedule at all.
Trying earlier-finishing candidates first finds a good incumbent sooner, strengthening later pruning.
Sorting candidates would entirely replace the role the lower bound is supposed to play.
why: 搜索顺序不改变正确性，但影响多快找到好的 best；好的 incumbent 会让 bound 剪更多分支。
why_en: Candidate ordering helps find a good incumbent early, making bound pruning more effective.

termDefinitions.meaning: 搜索过程中当前已知的最好完整解，后续分支要击败它才有意义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The incumbent is the best complete solution found so far, and later branches only matter if they can beat it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 排序本身不能证明任何东西，最优性是靠下界和穷举覆盖来保证的。
不排序候选顺序仍然可以产出合法 schedule，只是找到好解可能更慢。
先试完成得早的候选，能更快拿到一个不错的 incumbent，后面的下界比较就能更早剪掉更多分支。
排序只是影响探索顺序，下界该算还是要算，两者不能互相替代。
optionExplanations_en: Sorting by itself proves nothing -- optimality still comes from the bound plus exhaustive coverage.
Leaving candidates unsorted would still produce a legal schedule, it would just likely take longer to find a good one.
Trying earlier-finishing candidates first gets a decent incumbent sooner, so later bound comparisons can prune more branches earlier.
Sorting only changes exploration order; the bound still has to be computed regardless -- one doesn't replace the other.

scenario: 你要实现 lower bound 的 station 部分。
scenario_en: You are implementing the station component of the lower bound.
q: lower bound 里这段 station 循环代码在表达什么？
q_en: What does this station loop in the lower bound express?
options: station 至少要等到空闲时间，再串行做完剩余工作
每个 station 可以并行完成所有剩余工作
这段代码直接就是当前 best schedule
remaining 越大，makespan 反而越小
options_en: Each station must wait at least until it is free, then serially finish its remaining work.
Each station can finish all its remaining work in parallel.
This code snippet directly is the current best schedule.
A larger remaining value makes the makespan smaller.
codeSample:
for st in stations:
    bound = max(bound, station_free[i] + remaining[st])
why: station 独占约束提供了强下界；即使使用最快 chef，属于同一 station 的剩余工作也不能重叠。
why_en: The station component bounds completion time by current station availability plus its remaining fastest work.
whenOtherWins: 如果 station 没有独占限制，这个下界项就不成立。
tradeoff: 把 station 剩余工作当串行下界 vs 假设 station 能并行处理

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: 这段循环取的是「station 空闲时间 + 剩余工作」，意思是 station 至少要等到空出来，剩余工作还得排队做完，两者加起来是乐观下界。
station 一次只能服务一位厨师，不能并行处理剩余工作，这条不成立。
这只是下界计算的一部分，不是排好的 schedule 本身。
剩余工作量越大，做完所需时间只会越长，makespan 不会因此变小。
optionExplanations_en: This loop takes station free time plus remaining work -- meaning the station must at least wait until free, then serialize the rest, and that sum is the optimistic bound.
A station only serves one chef at a time and can't parallelize remaining work, so this doesn't hold.
This is just one term in a bound calculation, not an actual completed schedule.
More remaining work only ever takes longer to finish, it doesn't shrink the makespan.

scenario: 三 dish order 要达到 105 秒最优。
scenario_en: The three-dish order needs to reach the 105-second optimum.
q: 关键 ordering 变化是什么？
q_en: What is the key ordering change?
options: 让 Salad 拖到全部菜里最后才开始 prep 备料
把 Alice 从 GRILL 调去做 PREP 这个环节
让所有 dish 的 grill 步骤都统一推迟到 90 秒以后才开始
Pasta 提前 chop，正好接上 Burger 让出的 grill
options_en: Push Salad's prep to happen dead last, after every other dish.
Move Alice off GRILL and onto the PREP station instead.
Make every dish's grill step wait until after the 90-second mark to start.
Chop Pasta earlier so it is ready exactly when Burger frees the grill.
why: Pasta chop 30-60，Burger grill 15-60，Pasta grill 60-105，grill 没有空档；一个 swap 就追回 30 秒。
why_en: The optimal schedule gets Pasta ready for the grill exactly when Burger leaves it.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标只是按菜品顺序出餐而不是最短 makespan，可能不能这样重排。
tradeoff: 重排 chop 顺序、消除 grill 空档 vs 保持 greedy 的默认 dish 顺序
diagram:
flowchart LR
A[Prep all] --> B[Pasta chop early]
B --> C[Burger grill]
C --> D[Pasta grill immediately]
D --> E[Shorter makespan]

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: 把 Salad 拖到最后反而会让别的资源空等，帮不上这道 30 秒差距。
题目没有给出厨师和 station 的绑定细节，这个说法是编造的干扰项。
刻意让 grill 空等到 90 秒后才开工，正是要消除的浪费，不是解法。

options: 高估会让搜索直接变成 O(1) 且仍然正确
lower bound 只要越大越好，不管准不准
高估只会影响打印的顺序，无关正确性
高估可能把真正最优的分支剪掉，破坏最优性保证
options_en: Overestimating makes the search O(1) and still correct.
A lower bound just needs to be as large as possible, regardless of accuracy.
Overestimating only affects print order, not correctness.
Overestimating can prune away the truly optimal branch, breaking the optimality guarantee.
why: branch-and-bound 的正确性依赖下界不超过真实可达最优；激进但不安全的估计只能用于排序启发，不能用于硬剪枝。
why_en: An unsafe bound can prune the optimal branch, so it cannot be used for correctness-preserving pruning.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是启发式求近似解而不要求最优，非安全估计可以用于优先级排序。
tradeoff: 安全（从不高估）的 lower bound vs 激进但可能高估的估计

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

optionExplanations: 高估不会让搜索突然变成常数时间，反而会破坏它原本该有的正确性保证。
下界要的是「不超过真实最优」这条安全线，光是数值大没有意义，甚至有害。
高估影响的不只是打印顺序，它会直接改变哪些分支被剪掉。
如果这个估计偶尔比真实可达的最优值还大，就可能把包含真正最优解的分支提前剪掉，最优性保证也就没了。
optionExplanations_en: Overestimating doesn't magically make the search O(1); it breaks the correctness guarantee the bound is supposed to provide.
What a bound needs is to never exceed the true achievable optimum -- being merely large is meaningless, even harmful.
Overestimating affects far more than print order; it directly changes which branches get cut.
If this estimate sometimes exceeds the true achievable optimum, it can prune away the branch holding the actual best schedule, breaking the optimality guarantee.

scenario: 一个 step 要同时占用一个 chef 和一个 station，你要算它的最早合法开始时间。
scenario_en: A step occupies both a chef and a station at the same time, and you need to compute its earliest legal start time.
q: 为什么 station_free 和 chef_free 都要跟踪？
q_en: Why do we need to track both station_free and chef_free?
options: 只要 chef 空闲，就能在同一 station 上并行处理
station_free 这个状态只用来控制界面输出的颜色
step 同时占用一个 chef 和一个 station，任一未空闲都不能开始
chef_free 和 station_free 这两个状态在任何时刻都永远保持完全相同
options_en: As long as the chef is free, work can run on the station in parallel.
The station_free state is only used to control the color of the output display.
A step occupies one chef and one station together, and neither can be busy for it to start.
chef_free and station_free are always exactly identical.
why: chef 和 station 是两套独立资源约束，最早开始时间必须同时满足它们。
why_en: Each step requires both a chef and a station to be available.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: 厨师空闲不代表 station 也空闲，两者是各自独立的资源，不能只看一个。
station_free 直接参与最早开始时间的计算，跟输出怎么显示没关系。
一个 step 要同时占住一位厨师和一个 station，任何一个还没空出来，这一步都开始不了。
厨师和 station 是两套互不相关的资源状态，它们的空闲时间没有理由必须相等。
optionExplanations_en: A chef being free doesn't mean the station is -- they're two independent resources, and you can't just check one.
station_free feeds directly into computing the earliest start time; it has nothing to do with how output gets displayed.
A step needs to hold both one chef and one station at the same time, and if either isn't free yet, the step can't start.
Chef and station are two unrelated resource states, and there's no reason their free times would always match.

scenario: 你在为 branch-and-bound 设计递归状态，需要决定保留哪些字段。
scenario_en: You are designing the recursive state for branch-and-bound and need to decide which fields to keep.
q: search 状态里哪些数组或元组是必要的？
q_en: Which arrays or tuples are necessary in the search state?
options: next_step：每个 dish 走到第几步
dish_ready：每个 dish 下一步最早可开始时间
chef_free 和 station_free：资源空闲时间
随机数生成器状态，决定合法性
options_en: next_step: how far each dish has progressed.
dish_ready: the earliest a dish's next step can start.
chef_free and station_free: when each resource becomes available.
A random-number generator's state, which decides legality.
why: 这些状态共同决定当前可选 steps 和每个候选的开始/结束时间；随机数不是调度语义的一部分。
why_en: The search state must capture dish progress, dish readiness, and resource availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 dish 里下一个可以开始的 step，因为它前面的 step 都已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ready step is a dish's next step, eligible to run once every earlier step in that dish is done.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: next_step 记录每道菜走到第几步，决定接下来哪个 step 是 ready 的。
dish_ready 是这道菜下一步最早能开始的时间，算候选开始时间少不了它。
chef_free 和 station_free 分别记录两类资源什么时候空出来，是算合法开始时间的另外两个必要条件。
调度的合法性和最优性跟随机数毫无关系，这个状态不该出现在这里。
optionExplanations_en: next_step tracks how far each dish has progressed, which determines which step is ready next.
dish_ready is the earliest this dish's next step could start, and it's essential to computing candidate start times.
chef_free and station_free each record when their resource frees up -- the other two ingredients needed for a legal start time.
Legality and optimality of the schedule have nothing to do with a random number generator, so this state has no place here.

scenario: 搜索走到一半，partial schedule 已把部分 chef/station 占用到某个时刻，且不可撤销。
scenario_en: Midway through the search, the partial schedule has already booked some chefs and stations up to a point, and that can't be undone.
q: lower bound 的“当前资源最晚忙到时间”项为什么必要？
q_en: Why does the lower bound need the latest currently busy resource time?
options: 它会高估所有还没被安排进 schedule 里的剩余工作总量
schedule 不会早于已安排的 chef/station 完成时间结束
它替代了对 dish 内部前置关系所要做的完整检查流程
它只是用来给最终排出来的结果做一次 tie-break 排序而已，没别的用
options_en: It overestimates the total amount of work not yet placed into the schedule.
The schedule cannot finish earlier than its already-committed chef and station work.
It replaces the need for a full dish-precedence check.
It's only ever used to tie-break the ordering of the final printed result, nothing more.
why: 已有 partial schedule 的资源占用已经不可逆，makespan 至少要等当前最晚的已安排工作完成。
why_en: The final makespan cannot be earlier than the latest currently occupied resource time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 这一项只看已经排定、不可撤销的工作，跟还没安排的部分没关系，谈不上高估未排工作。
已经安排好的厨师和 station 工作不能撤销，最终 makespan 不可能早于这些已提交工作的完成时间。
dish 前置关系是单独一项检查，这一项管的是资源占用，两者互不替代。
它是下界计算的一部分，直接参与判断分支要不要剪，不只是拿来排序展示。
optionExplanations_en: This term only looks at already-committed, irreversible work, not anything unscheduled, so it isn't overestimating future work.
Already-committed chef and station work can't be undone, so the final makespan can never finish earlier than that committed work completes.
Dish precedence is checked separately; this term is about resource occupancy, and one doesn't substitute for the other.
It's part of the bound calculation and directly decides whether a branch gets pruned, not just something used for display ordering.

scenario: 订单很小、target 很宽松，只要求尽快交一个合法排程。
scenario_en: The order is small, the target is loose, and you only need to return a legal schedule quickly.
q: 哪种方案可能最合适？
q_en: Which approach is likely the best fit?
options: 简单的 dish-order greedy 或 dispatch 就够用
上完整的 branch-and-bound 搜索找最优
手动建模成 integer programming 再交给专门的求解器
跳过 recipe 顺序检查，直接乱序排
options_en: Plain dish-order greedy or dispatch is enough.
Run a full branch-and-bound search for the optimum.
Model it as integer programming and hand it to a solver.
Skip the recipe-order check and schedule in any order.
why: 简单 greedy 能快速产出合法 schedule；只有当 makespan target 紧或 greedy 结构性失败时，搜索成本才合理。
why_en: A greedy scheduler is pragmatic when feasibility matters more than optimal makespan.
whenOtherWins: 在本文硬 benchmarks 中，greedy 和 dispatch 都 miss targets，必须用 bounded search。
tradeoff: 简单合法但可能不是最优 vs 保证最优但实现/运行成本更高

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and assigns each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把调度约束写成整数变量的约束，交给通用求解器求最优的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Integer programming encodes the scheduling constraints as integer-variable constraints and hands them to a general-purpose solver for the optimum.

optionExplanations: 订单小、目标又宽松时，简单的 greedy 或 dispatch 几步就能给出合法排程，不值得多花实现和运行成本。
完整搜索能保证最优，但对这种小规模宽松场景是杀鸡用牛刀，调优成本换不来收益。
接入通用求解器的建模和运维成本更高，对一个宽松、快出解的场景没必要。
跳过 recipe 顺序检查会直接产出非法排程，不管场景多宽松都不能这么做。
optionExplanations_en: When the order is small and the target loose, plain greedy or dispatch produces a legal schedule in a few steps -- not worth the extra implementation and runtime cost of more.
Full search guarantees optimality, but for a small, loose-target case that's overkill -- the tuning cost doesn't pay for itself here.
Wiring up a general-purpose solver adds modeling and operational overhead that a loose, fast-turnaround case doesn't need.
Skipping the recipe-order check produces an illegal schedule outright, no matter how loose the target is -- never acceptable.

scenario: 改版后 non-specialist 只比 specialist 慢一点，而且 station specialist 排队很严重。
scenario_en: After a rule change, non-specialists are only slightly slower than specialists, and station specialists have long queues.
q: 原来的“只用 fastest chef”剪枝可能有什么问题？
q_en: What can go wrong with the original fastest-chef-only pruning?
options: 这条剪枝规则在新条件下依旧永远能保持绝对安全，不受影响
可能错过稍慢 chef 反而更早完成、makespan 更低的 schedule
会让 lower bound 变得更紧一点，而且完全不会影响到任何最优性保证
会自动切换成枚举所有 chef 组合方式的更慢搜索模式
options_en: This pruning rule stays perfectly safe under the new conditions no matter what, unaffected.
It could miss a legal schedule where a slightly slower chef actually finishes earlier and lowers makespan.
It makes the lower bound tighter without affecting optimality.
It automatically switches to enumerating every chef combination.
why: specialist rule 是利用本文具体速度结构的 dominated-choice 剪枝；速度结构变了，就要重新验证是否安全。
why_en: The fastest-chef simplification is only safe when non-specialists are truly dominated.
whenOtherWins: 在原文三倍慢的 chef 配置下，折叠 chef choice 可以显著减小搜索树。
tradeoff: 折叠 chef 选择、只搜 ordering vs 重新把 chef 选择纳入搜索空间

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 station 上速度是 0.5 factor 的 chef，比其余 1.5 factor 的 chef 快三倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialist is the one chef who runs a given station at half the base time, three times faster than a non-specialist there.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在给定结构下必然不比另一个候选更优，可以直接排除而不影响最优解的选项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dominated choice can never beat another option given the problem's structure, so it can be excluded without affecting optimality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 这条剪枝之所以安全，靠的是「non-specialist 永远慢很多」这个前提，前提一变就不能再假设它永远成立。
如果 non-specialist 只慢一点、specialist 又排长队，稍慢的厨师反而可能更早接手，把它剪掉就会漏掉更优的 schedule。
剪枝本身不会让下界自动变紧，它是直接排除了一部分候选，跟下界计算是两回事。
剪枝规则不会自己感知场景变化去切换策略，得由人重新判断并调整代码。
optionExplanations_en: This pruning rule is only safe because non-specialists were always assumed much slower -- once that premise changes, it can't be assumed to hold anymore.
If non-specialists are only slightly slower and specialists have long queues, a slightly slower chef could actually pick up the step sooner, and pruning it away would miss a better schedule.
Pruning doesn't automatically tighten the bound -- it just excludes some candidates outright, a different mechanism from bound computation.
A pruning rule doesn't sense the scenario changing and switch strategies on its own -- someone has to re-verify it and adjust the code.

scenario: symmetry cut 靠合并等价 dish 来减少分支，但搜索仍必须返回真正的最优 makespan。
scenario_en: The symmetry cut merges equivalent dishes to cut branches, but the search must still return the true optimal makespan.
q: symmetry cut 如果把 ready time 不同的相同 recipe dishes 合并，会有什么风险？
q_en: What is the risk if a symmetry cut merges same-recipe dishes with different ready times?
options: 只会让搜索的正确性更有保障
会让 station_free 的计算变得更准确
它们并不等价，可能剪掉更优 schedule 的分支
对结果完全没有任何影响
options_en: It can only make the search's correctness more solid.
It makes the station_free calculation more accurate.
They are not truly equivalent, so it may prune away a better schedule.
It has absolutely no effect on the result at all.
why: 可互换性要求 recipe、step index 和 ready time 等状态都相同；少一个条件就可能错误合并。
why_en: Symmetry pruning is safe only when the dishes are identical in all state relevant to future scheduling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

optionExplanations: 少了 ready time 这个条件，合并出来的候选其实并不等价，正确性反而会被破坏。
这个剪枝跟 station_free 怎么算没有关系，它管的是要不要展开某个分支。
recipe 相同但 ready time 不同意味着两道菜其实不可互换，把它们当等价剪掉，可能正好剪掉了藏着更优解的那条分支。
合并了不该合并的状态会实实在在改变搜索结果，不是没有影响。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping the ready-time condition means the merged candidates aren't actually equivalent, and that breaks correctness rather than helping it.
This pruning has nothing to do with how station_free gets computed -- it's about whether to expand a branch at all.
Same recipe but different ready times means the dishes aren't truly interchangeable, and treating them as equivalent can prune away exactly the branch holding the better schedule.
Merging states that shouldn't be merged genuinely changes the search outcome -- it's not a no-op.

q: 填空：prep_bottleneck_seven 的 target 是 {{195}}，greedy {{255}}，dispatch {{240}}，search {{195}}。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: prep_bottleneck_seven has target {{195}}, greedy {{255}}, dispatch {{240}}, and search {{195}}.
why: dispatch 从 255 降到 240 仍未达标，只有 search 命中 195 的目标，说明瓶颈是 ordering，不是局部规则不够聪明。
why_en: On prep_bottleneck_seven, dispatch improves but still misses the target, and only search reaches the optimum of 195.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从调度开始到最后一个 step 完成的总耗时，是要最小化的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Makespan is the total time from the start of scheduling until the last step finishes, and it's the value being minimized.

scenario: 你要把 Kitchen Orders 的经验迁移到下一道 ordering 才是瓶颈的排程题上。
scenario_en: You want to carry the Kitchen Orders lessons into the next scheduling problem where ordering is the real bottleneck.
q: Kitchen Orders 的主要 takeaways 有哪些？
q_en: What are the main takeaways from Kitchen Orders?
options: 先区分合法 schedule 和好 schedule
当 ordering 是瓶颈时，单向 greedy 往往不够
安全 lower bound、memo、dominated choices、symmetry 可以让指数搜索可用
只要选最快 chef，就一定全局最优
options_en: First separate a valid schedule from a good one.
When ordering is the bottleneck, a one-pass greedy rule usually is not enough.
A safe lower bound, a memo, dominated choices, and symmetry make exponential search usable.
Just always picking the fastest chef guarantees the global optimum.
why: 最快 chef 是必要但不充分；文章真正的经验是用结构化剪枝把 ordering 搜索控制住。
why_en: The lesson is to turn a hard ordering problem into a bounded search using safe pruning and problem structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存已搜索过的等价状态与当时的下界，命中时跳过重复搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memo caches equivalent states already searched along with the bound seen then, so the search can skip duplicate work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在给定结构下必然不比另一个候选更优，可以直接排除而不影响最优解的选项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dominated choice can never beat another option given the problem's structure, so it can be excluded without affecting optimality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

optionExplanations: 先保证排程合法，再谈怎么排得更好，这是文章反复强调的第一原则。
当瓶颈出在 ordering 上时，不管规则设计得多聪明，单向不可撤销的 greedy 往往追不上真正的最优解。
安全下界砍掉没希望的分支、memo 避免重复搜索、dominated choice 折叠 chef 维度、symmetry cut 去掉对称子树——四者一起才把指数级搜索压到能跑的规模。
永远选最快厨师只是必要条件，不足以保证全局最优——本题的 30 秒差距恰恰来自顺序，不是厨师选择。
optionExplanations_en: Get the schedule legal first, then worry about making it good -- the article keeps coming back to this as the first principle.
When the bottleneck is ordering, a one-pass, no-undo greedy rule usually can't catch up to the true optimum, no matter how cleverly it's designed.

A safe lower bound cuts hopeless branches, a memo avoids repeated search, dominated choices collapse the chef dimension, and a symmetry cut removes duplicate subtrees -- together they bring exponential search down to a runnable size.
Always picking the fastest chef is necessary but not sufficient for global optimality -- this example's 30-second gap comes from ordering, not chef choice.

scenario: 你要把这个题归到 Backtracking 模式。
scenario_en: You need to classify this problem under the Backtracking pattern.
q: 最准确的解释是什么？
q_en: What is the most accurate explanation?
options: 因为整个调度问题从头到尾只需要一次排序操作就能结束
每次选一个 ready step 递归剩余，再用 bound 剪掉无望子树
因为它本质上其实完全等价于对一张无向图做一次 BFS 广度优先搜索遍历
因为它只靠一个哈希集合做去重处理就已经完全足够了
options_en: Because the whole scheduling problem finishes from start to end with just a single sort.
It picks one ready step, recurses on what remains, and prunes hopeless subtrees with a bound.
Because it is, in essence, equivalent to running a single BFS traversal over an undirected graph.
Because a single hash set for deduplication is already completely sufficient on its own.
why: 第三版就是搜索解空间树：尝试一个选择，进入更小问题，用剪枝控制爆炸；这是典型 backtracking/branch-and-bound。
why_en: The final scheduler is backtracking over ready-step choices with branch-and-bound pruning.
whenOtherWins: 如果一个局部规则已经能保证目标，greedy pattern 会更轻。
tradeoff: 递归试探+剪枝（backtracking） vs 一次排序/BFS 之类的单趟算法

termDefinitions.meaning: 尝试一个选择、递归到更小问题、行不通就撤销再试下一个候选的搜索模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking tries one choice, recurses into the smaller remaining problem, and undoes the choice to try the next candidate when a branch fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 dish 里下一个可以开始的 step，因为它前面的 step 都已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ready step is a dish's next step, eligible to run once every earlier step in that dish is done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 一次排序解决不了排程问题，makespan 取决于组合选择，不是一个静态顺序就能定的。
每次从 ready step 里选一个、砍掉不可能更优的分支、递归解决剩下的子问题，这正是这版调度器的搜索方式。
这里没有图遍历意义上的节点和边，BFS 这个说法不成立。
光靠一个哈希集合去重解决不了要不要展开某个分支这个问题，还需要下界配合。
optionExplanations_en: A single sort can't solve this scheduling problem -- makespan depends on combinatorial choices, not a static order.
Pick one ready step, cut any branch that can't possibly beat the best, and recurse on what's left -- that's how this scheduler searches.
There's no graph of nodes and edges being traversed here, so calling it BFS doesn't hold up.
A hash set for deduplication alone can't decide whether to expand a branch -- that still needs the bound working alongside it.

scenario: 三个调度器都产出合法 schedule，但只有第三个把 makespan 压进 target 以内。
scenario_en: All three schedulers produce valid schedules, but only the third one pushes makespan inside the target.
q: “make it valid”和“make it good”在本文中分别对应什么？
q_en: What do “make it valid” and “make it good” mean in this problem?
options: valid 专指整个排程必须用 Alice；good 专指必须用 Bob 这个 chef
valid 满足 recipe/chef/station 三类约束；good 要把 makespan 压到达标
valid 是指直接返回一个完全空的 schedule；good 则是指干脆彻底无视掉 station 约束
两者其实完全同义，只是文章换了一种说法表达而已
options_en: Valid specifically means the whole schedule must use Alice; good specifically means it must use Bob.
Valid satisfies the recipe, chef, and station constraints; good pushes makespan down to the targets.
Valid here means returning a completely empty schedule; good means simply ignoring the station constraint.
They mean exactly the same thing, just different wording in the article.
why: 前两个 greedy 都能 make it valid，但 misses targets；search 负责 make it good。
why_en: A valid schedule respects constraints, while a good one minimizes makespan enough to meet targets.
tradeoff: valid（约束合法）vs good（makespan 达标/最优）

termDefinitions.meaning: 从调度开始到最后一个 step 完成的总耗时，是要最小化的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Makespan is the total time from the start of scheduling until the last step finishes, and it's the value being minimized.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一道 dish 内部固定顺序的 station step 链，后一步必须等前一步完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recipe is a dish's fixed chain of station steps, where each step must wait for the previous one to finish.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: 题目里没有规定谁必须用某个具体厨师，这个说法是编造的。
valid 指满足 recipe、chef、station 这些约束，good 指把 makespan 压到达标甚至最优，两者是完全不同的两条标准。
空 schedule 或忽略约束都直接违反 valid 的要求，跟这两个概念的定义对不上。
两者标准明显不同——前两版 greedy 已经做到 valid，却依然 miss targets，说明 good 是更高的一层要求。
optionExplanations_en: Nothing in the setup requires any specific chef to be used -- that claim is invented.
Valid means satisfying the recipe, chef, and station constraints; good means pushing makespan down to meet or beat the targets -- two entirely different bars.
An empty schedule or ignoring a constraint both directly violate what 'valid' requires, so this doesn't match either definition.
The two clearly differ -- both earlier greedy passes already achieve valid, yet still miss the targets, which is exactly why good is a higher bar.

scenario: 你看完全部 benchmark 结果，要用一句话总结三种调度器的整体表现。
scenario_en: After reviewing all benchmark results, you need to summarize the three schedulers in one sentence.
q: benchmark 总结哪项正确？
q_en: Which benchmark summary is correct?
options: dispatch 命中每一个 target，而 search 反而在全部 case 上超时失败
greedy/dispatch 全错过 target；search 全中，约 928ms
greedy 单独一个就已经命中了所有 case 的 target
三种方法在所有 case 上都统一输出 105 这个结果
options_en: Dispatch hits every single target while search times out on all of them instead.
Greedy and dispatch miss every target; search hits all of them in about 928ms.
Greedy alone already hits the target on every case.
All three methods output 105 on every single case.
why: 表格的结论是更好的 one-pass rule 仍不够；只有 branch-and-bound search 在所有 case 上达到目标。
why_en: The benchmark shows that only branch-and-bound search reaches every makespan target.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and assigns each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从调度开始到最后一个 step 完成的总耗时，是要最小化的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Makespan is the total time from the start of scheduling until the last step finishes, and it's the value being minimized.

optionExplanations: 这个说法把结果说反了——真正全部超时的从来不是 search。
两版 greedy 每个用例都没达标，唯独搜索版全部命中，哪怕是最大规模也只要约 928 毫秒就能跑完。
greedy 在多个用例上其实是没达标的，deep_nine 就明显超出目标。
105 秒只是三道菜用例的目标，其它规模的用例目标各不相同，不会到处都是 105。
optionExplanations_en: This has it backwards -- it's never search that times out here.
Both greedy passes fall short on every case, but the search version nails all of them, finishing even the largest in about 928 milliseconds.
Greedy actually falls short on several cases, deep_nine being the clearest miss.
105 seconds is only the target for the three-dish case -- other sizes have their own different targets, not 105 everywhere.

scenario: 三道菜的第一步都是 PREP;PREP 专家 Carol 做一个 prep 只要 15 秒,另两位 chef 要 45 秒,且一个 station 同一时刻只容一个 chef。
scenario_en: All three dishes start with a PREP step; PREP specialist Carol runs one prep in 15s, the other two chefs take 45s, and a station holds one chef at a time.
q: 任何调度器能把这三个 prep 压到多快?
q_en: How fast can any scheduler make these three preps finish?
options: 45 秒:三个 15 秒 prep 只能在 Carol 上排队
15 秒:三个 prep 在 Carol 上可以并行同时开跑
30 秒:把两个 prep 分给别的 chef 就能并行追平
不定:prep 段耗时要等 GRILL 怎么排才能确定
options_en: 45s: the three 15s preps can only queue on Carol.
15s: the three preps can run in parallel on Carol at once.
30s: hand two preps to other chefs and parallelism ties it.
It depends: the prep span is only fixed once GRILL is laid out.
why: PREP station 一次只容一个 chef,三个 prep 都归专家 Carol,只能串行,15×3=45 秒无法压缩;这 45 秒直接成为 station 下界的一部分。
why_en: All three preps go to specialist Carol and a station holds one chef at a time, so they serialize to 15×3 = 45s no matter the order -- that floor feeds the station lower bound.
optionExplanations: 对:station 独占加专家唯一,三个 prep 只能一个接一个,45 秒是硬地板。
并行要多个 station 实例,PREP 只有一个 station,同一时刻只能跑一个。
别的 chef 做一个 prep 要 45 秒,分出去反而更慢,追不平 Carol 的 15 秒。
这 45 秒下界不依赖 GRILL 怎么排,prep 段自身就已经确定。
optionExplanations_en: Right: station exclusivity plus a single specialist forces the three preps to run one after another; 45s is a hard floor.
Parallelism needs multiple station instances, but PREP has one station that runs one step at a time.
Another chef needs 45s per prep, so offloading is slower and can't match Carol's 15s.
This 45s bound doesn't depend on how GRILL is arranged; the prep span is fixed on its own.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一类工位(PREP/CHOP/GRILL),同一时刻只容一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station is a work post (PREP/CHOP/GRILL) that holds only one chef at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个 station 半速的那位 chef,别的 chef 在该 station 慢三倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The specialist is the chef who runs a given station at half time, while the others are three times slower there.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对剩余最优 makespan 的乐观、不高估的估计,用来剪枝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best remaining makespan, used to prune.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从调度开始到最后一个 step 完成的总耗时,要最小化的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Makespan is the total time until the last step finishes, the value being minimized.

scenario: branch-and-bound 用 memo 记录见过的状态。有人想把 key 简化成只用 canonical(每个 dish 的进度和 ready time),丢掉 chef_free / station_free 两个资源向量。
scenario_en: The branch-and-bound memo records seen states. Someone wants to shrink the key to just canonical (each dish's progress and ready time), dropping the chef_free / station_free resource vectors.
q: 只用 canonical 当 memo key 会怎么坏?
q_en: How does keying the memo on canonical alone break?
options: 同进度但资源空闲时刻不同的状态被合并,memo 误剪掉更优分支,makespan 偏大
key 太短会永远命中不了任何状态,memo 形同虚设,搜索退化成无剪枝指数树
canonical 已含 ready time,资源忙到几点由它唯一确定,去掉不影响正确性
去掉资源向量后 lower bound 会算错,搜索会报告一个非法的 schedule
options_en: States with equal progress but different resource-free times get merged, so the memo prunes a better branch and the makespan comes out too large.
Too short a key never hits any state, so the memo does nothing and the search degrades to an unpruned exponential tree.
Canonical already has ready time, which uniquely fixes when resources free up, so dropping the vectors is safe.
Without the resource vectors the lower bound miscomputes and the search reports an illegal schedule.
why: canonical 只记 dish 进度,不含 chef/station 忙到几点;两个进度相同但资源空闲时刻不同的状态并不等价,合并会误剪更优分支,让搜索返回偏大的 makespan。
why_en: Canonical captures dish progress but not when chefs and stations free up, so merging states that differ only in resource times prunes a better branch and returns a too-large makespan.
optionExplanations: 对:资源忙到几点决定后续能多早开工,不进 key 就会错误等价两个状态。
key 短只会让更多状态碰撞合并,不是命不中;命不中反而没有正确性风险。
canonical 里的 ready time 是 dish 自己的,推不出 chef/station 各自忙到几点。
lower bound 用的是实参 chef_free/station_free,不看 memo key,不会因此产出非法结果。
optionExplanations_en: Right: when resources free up decides how early later steps can start, so leaving it out of the key wrongly equates two states.
A short key causes more collisions and merges, not misses; a miss would actually be safe.
Ready time in canonical is per dish and can't recover when each chef/station is busy until.
The lower bound reads the actual chef_free/station_free arguments, not the memo key, so it won't produce an illegal result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存已到达状态见过的最好下界,重复且不更优的状态直接跳过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The memo caches the best bound seen at each reached state so equal-or-worse repeats are skipped.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可互换 dish 归一化后的状态签名:各 dish 的 signature、进度、ready time 排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Canonical is a normalized state signature: each dish's recipe signature, progress, and ready time, sorted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录每个 chef 忙到哪一刻的向量,决定他下一步最早能几点开工。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: chef_free is a vector of when each chef is busy until, deciding the earliest they can start next.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录每个 station 忙到哪一刻的向量,与 chef_free 共同约束最早开始时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: station_free is a vector of when each station is busy until, constraining the earliest start alongside chef_free.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对剩余最优 makespan 的乐观、不高估的估计,用来剪枝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best remaining makespan.

scenario: lower_bound 有一项 dish 下界 = dish_ready 加上该 dish 从当前步到末步、按最快 chef 算的剩余时间。lower_bound 在搜索的每个节点都被调用一次。
scenario_en: One term of lower_bound is a dish bound = dish_ready plus that dish's remaining time from the current step to the end, timed at the fastest chef. lower_bound runs at every search node.
q: 这个剩余时间怎么算才不拖慢热路径?
q_en: How should that remaining time be computed to not slow the hot path?
options: 开局对每个 dish 逆序前缀和预算出 tail[],之后查 tail[step] 就是 O(1)
每次进 lower_bound 都从当前步到末步现场累加 fastest_dur,步数不多没关系
把剩余时间也塞进 memo key,用哈希查表代替每次求和
只用第一步的时间做近似,忽略后面的步以省下计算量
options_en: Precompute tail[] once per dish as a reverse prefix sum, then tail[step] is an O(1) lookup.
Re-sum fastest_dur from the current step to the end inside every lower_bound call; steps are few.
Put the remaining time into the memo key too and hash-lookup instead of summing.
Approximate with just the first step's time and ignore later steps to save work.
why: tail[d][si] 是 fastest_dur 从 si 到末步的逆序前缀和,开局 O(steps) 建一次;lower_bound 在每个搜索节点都跑,查表把 dish 下界从 O(steps) 降到 O(1)。
why_en: tail[d][si] is a reverse prefix sum of the fastest durations from step si onward, built once, so the dish bound is an O(1) lookup at every search node instead of an O(steps) resum.
tradeoff: 一次性 O(steps) 建表加一点内存 vs 热路径每次查表 O(1) 省时
whenOtherWins: 如果 lower_bound 只调用一两次,现场累加就够,预计算反而多一步建表;只有它在每个节点反复跑,O(1) 查表才值回预算。
optionExplanations: 对:逆序前缀和让 dish 下界变成查表,建表只花一次 O(steps)。
现场累加每个节点都 O(steps),乘上指数级节点数就成了热路径瓶颈。
剩余时间随 next_step 变,塞进 key 会撑爆状态空间,不是省算的办法。
只算第一步会低估剩余,下界不再安全,可能剪掉真正的最优解。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the reverse prefix sum turns the dish bound into a lookup; the table costs one O(steps) build.
On-the-fly summing is O(steps) per node, and times an exponential node count it becomes the hot-path cost.
Remaining time varies with next_step, so folding it into the key blows up the state space rather than saving work.
Using only the first step underestimates the remainder, making the bound unsafe and able to prune the true optimum.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀和:预累加数组,使区间求和变成一次查表 O(1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prefix sum is a pre-accumulated array that turns a range sum into a single O(1) lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 step 交给该 station 最快 chef 时的耗时,预先算好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: fastest_dur is each step's duration when run by that station's fastest chef, precomputed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对剩余最优 makespan 的乐观、不高估的估计,用来剪枝。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best remaining makespan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常数时间:操作耗时与输入规模无关,如一次数组查表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means constant time -- the cost doesn't grow with input size, like one array lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性于步数:耗时随该 dish 的 step 数量成正比增长。
termDefinitions.fullName: Order of the number of steps (linear time)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(steps) means the cost grows linearly with the number of steps in the dish.

scenario: benchmark 里 dispatch 在忙碌 order 上比 greedy 好(six-dish 225 降到 210),但在三个小 order 上和 dish-order greedy 逐字打平:135、165、195,且都没命中 target。
scenario_en: In the benchmarks dispatch beats greedy on busy orders (six-dish 225 to 210) but ties dish-order greedy exactly on the three small orders -- 135, 165, 195 -- and both miss every target.
q: 这个打平说明了什么?
q_en: What does that exact tie tell you?
options: 小 order 没有可交错的 ready step,dispatch 退化成 greedy;单向规则再聪明也不够
dispatch 实现里有 bug,正确实现应当在小 order 上也严格优于 greedy 才对
打平只是巧合,把每个 target 稍微调低一点这三个小 order 其实 dispatch 就能命中,并非结构问题
说明 greedy 在小 order 上已经是最优的,只有更大规模的 order 才需要搜索去改进
options_en: Small orders leave no ready steps to interleave, so dispatch degenerates to greedy; a smarter one-pass rule isn't enough.
There's a bug in dispatch; a correct implementation should strictly beat greedy on small orders too.
The tie is a coincidence; lower the target a little and dispatch would hit these three -- not a structural issue.
It shows greedy is already optimal on small orders, and only larger orders need search to improve on it.
why: 小 order 步骤少,没有可交错的 ready step,dispatch 无从重排,逐字等于 greedy。打平(不是仅仅差一点)证明换更聪明的单向规则也补不上缺口,只能上 branch-and-bound 搜索。
why_en: With few steps to interleave, dispatch reorders nothing and ties greedy exactly at 135/165/195; that exact tie, not a near miss, is the tell that no one-pass rule suffices and you need search.
optionExplanations: 对:没有可交错的步,dispatch 就是 greedy,打平暴露了单向规则的天花板。
两版都是干净的单向 greedy,没有 bug;差别只在何时提交,不在实现对错。
target 是给定的最优 makespan,不能为了让 dispatch 好看去调低它。
greedy 在小 order 上也没命中 target(135 对 105),远不是最优。
optionExplanations_en: Right: with no steps to interleave, dispatch is just greedy, and the tie exposes the ceiling of one-pass rules.
Both are clean single-pass greedy with no bug; they differ only in when they commit, not in correctness.
The target is the given optimal makespan; you can't lower it just to make dispatch look good.
Greedy misses the target on small orders too (135 vs 105), so it's far from optimal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, finishes earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and gives each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个未完成 dish 当前可运行的那一步,即它 recipe 里的下一步。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ready step is the currently runnable step of an unfinished dish -- its next step in recipe order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 该 order 已知的最优 makespan,作为判定成败的给定标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The target is the order's known optimal makespan, the given yardstick for success.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能更优分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of orderings while pruning any branch that can't beat the current best.
